Composition rights
Commons’ blanket expiry metadata is unreliable: it gives the wrong composer death year. Disputed: sources disagree

Stravinsky died in 1971, not 1936. The 1910 score is described as public domain in the United States by the score catalogue, but not generally in life-plus-70 jurisdictions. The US government-work status of a band transcription or recording does not remove rights in the underlying composition.

  • Commons applies PD-old-auto-expired with deathyear=1936.
  • Stravinsky died in 1971; the 1910 score has territory-dependent copyright status, not blanket life-plus-70 expiry.

Recording rights
Rule 1 — recording-specific public-domain release: PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marine (US-law basis). Documented

Commons expressly applies PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marine to the recording or official federal-government performance, not only to the composition. Under 17 U.S.C. § 105(a), official US Government works are not protected by US copyright. This is rule 1’s recording-specific public-domain release route, not rule 2’s publication-date route; it does not establish worldwide public-domain status.
